x: As a result of the race, three of our walkers were selected to represent Middlesex at Southport, George Checkley 9th, Bob Newson 11th and Hugh McGreechan 12th.

We learned on the train that Hugh McGreechan had become engaged about 48 hours previously and he promised to pay for a round on the journey home, but I think he must have forgotten or else he's saving up.

Congratulations to George Checkley on taking third place in both the Metropolitan and the National Police 10 miles Championships. Also to Hugh McGreechan and Len Demmon who finished 4th and 5th in the Police "National".

Our team position had weakened a little for Hugh McGreechan was having his unaccountable day off which happens to everyone once in a life time and had gone back places, which had not yet been recovered by our other men.

We hail a new 20 Miles Club Champion in George Checkley who stunned us all after his recent form, by taking the lead at the start and tenaciously holding on to the end despite a grand challenge from the holder, Hugh McGreechan.
Bob Newson and Hugh McGreechan held their positions right through and Bob certainly earns credit for finishing 4th in 2hrs. 36mins. 53secs. Mac was 5th in 2.37.29 and Len Demmon 10th in 2.44.45.

Hugh McGreechan was well up all the way followed by Bob Newson with Beecham and Norman a little way back. After a bad spell on the homeward journey, Mac recovered and beat George Coleman near home for 5th place.

George Checkley cut out a fast pace, dogged by Hugh McGreechan and although Hugh challenged strongly all the way, George tenaciously held on to win in 2hrs. 54mins.22secs. with Mac 2.54.54, a splendid effort.

At the moment most of our distance men have a Middlesex qualification and our team consisted of George, Bob Newson, Hugh McGreechan, Len Demmon, Bob Readman, Fred Rolfe and Cyril Yescombe, and of course Harry Shields.

It is rumoured that the Surrey 10 will be held from our headquarters at Wimbledon so let's have a realy good team to make sure of hanging on to the title. Hugh McGreechan has sent me the following letter of thanks for his wedding present:

Eric Hall walked an excellent race in the 2 miles to finish 2nd to R, Goodall in 15 mins. with Ted Smith 3rd in 15.18. George Beecham 8th and H.McGreechan 10th were our scorers in the 5 miles, George Oliver 10th in the 4 miles and R, Newson 6th and L.

George Checkley 7th and Hugh McGreechan 9th, looked pretty good packing, but unfortunately our fourth man, Cyril Yescombe, who is quite a newcomer to distance racing, although making a brave effort, could do no better than 27th, which lost us 2nd team place by one point.

At Croydon Norman Guilmant was 4thm George Beecham, very fit after his holiday 5th, Hugh McGreechan 7th, Harry Shields 20th and Bernard 23rd, with Fred Rolfe, Bert Stallardm Ron Fairman, Joe Wilson and George Oliver coming along behind.
Hugh McGreechan won the Police Barking to Southend Race for the fourth time. Cyril Yescombe was 10th and won the handicap.
Syd James and Hugh McGreechan finished together in 1h. 44m. and Len Demmon and Trevor Luck certainly walked well. Harry Shields, with an allowance of 12 minutes, won the handicap.

A trio of Hugh McGreechan, Bob Newson and Norman Guilmant were at this time some three minutes behind with George Beecham, Harry Shields and Cyril Yescombe completing the team a further 2 minutes back.

Behind these two an interesting battle was going on for third place between Bob Newson, Hugh McGreechan and Norman Guilmant. The last named tried hard to steal a lead but Bob and Hugh would not let him get away.

Names like Fred Rickards, Fred Bentley, and Jack Bidgood remind us of the past years, but now it would seem that George Checkley and Hugh McGreechan have taken on the task of keeping a Belgrave name on the trophy.
From the start Bob Newson and Hugh McGreechan walked a steady race followed by George Beecham and Harry Shields with Fred Rolfe bringing up the rear.

Ably supported by George Checkley, 6th, Hugh McGreechan 10th and Harry Shields 12th, who enjoyed the last eight miles more than any other part of the race, we easily gained team honours with 18 points to Poly's 36 and Essex Beagles 41.
George Beecham, who needs the sun, had to give it best at 29 miles and Hugh McGreechan who had just come off night duty also found it too much and retired.

… 8th September, but the loss of Bob Newson due to the illness of his wife, was followed on the morning of the race when Hugh McGreechan, for some unaccountable reason, failed to turn up, which meant that two of our strongest distance walkers were absent.…

…ude's effort in gaining 2nd. place in the individual handicap,John Knifton 46th,Trevor Luck 37th (just outside 1hr.)and Hugh McGreechan's showing of some of his old form.Our older members performed well;Charlie Speechley,now 67years old,was 99th,Fred Brinning,after a lapse of a few years,was out aga…
Our fourth man, Hugh McGreechan lost several places in the last two miles but our margin over the third club, Polytechnic H., was always an appreciable one.
George Checkley walked soundly throughout, never seeming to falter; Bob Newson was a powerful third man and Hugh McGreechan prevailed over George Beecham for fourth position.
Meanwhile, George Beecham, revelling in the sunshine, came through to fourth with Hugh McGreechan and Bob Newson completing our scoring team in 6th and 7th positions.
Hugh McGreechan was 4th in 3h.49m.38s., Bob Newson 5th in 3.52.27, George Checkley 11th in 4.0.42, Bernard Eglinten 12th in 4.3.21, Fred Rolfe 15th in 4.7.35 and Harry Shields 16th in 4.8.12.

Our team was completed by Hugh McGreechan, in twelfth position, who walked a typically sound race. Four men in twelve is normally good enough to win a Championship and so it was, and our third successive win was accomplished.
However, form had altered very little for Ray Hall, Hugh McGreechan and George Beecham, 3rd, 4th and 5th last year, filled the first three places this time in the same order!
He capped a grand season by finishing 3rd, followed by George Beecham fifth and Hugh McGreechan tenth. These three occupying the first three places in the Club Championships, held in conjunction.
With our police friends we won the match, one of the highlights being the battle between George Beecham and Hugh McGreechan, with George taking 3rd place and the Irish Ash Tray.

Ted Smith, Hugh McGreechan and Charlie Walker are the proud fathers of newly born sons, whilst John Keown and Eric Gebbett and Jumbo Masters are equally proud of their daughters---perhaps we'll have a ladies section yet !

Vaughan Thomas won the first from Sandy Law and Hugh McGreechan and also the scratch race in the good time of 14:38. In a combined match with Surrey W.C. the Bels won, 121-132.
Congratulations to Hugh McGreechan on winning the Surrey W.C. 14 miles Keston race and also winning the Police Long Distance Championship - Barking to Southend - for the third time. .....
